main_body: Grey steel safe: a light-grey body with a dark outline, a big inset door frame holding a yellow dial and handle, and a base strip.
top_band: Rows 10-12 light grey (L=170), then a row-13 highlight (L=215) and rows 14-15 mid grey (L=126). Row 16 is the dark outline of the door frame. The top band is in the same lightness family as the front face (L=170 at x=4).
evidence: The upper 3 rows read as a thin cap on a flat front view, about 3 of 22 rows. At x=4 the top (L=170) and the front face (L=170) are the same tone, so the top is not separated from the face by a tone step. Only a highlight line and a dark outline mark the edge. The door and dial are drawn face-on. The inset door frame is the only 3/4-like cue, and it is not enough to read the main body as a top surface plus a front face. This is a front elevation with a hat, so it fails.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 10 distinct colours and a median of 10 colours per tile, against 38-40 distinct colours and 17-20 per tile in the references. All its dark edge pixels are neutral (100%), a near-black sticker outline, while the references use tinted outlines. It has only about 4 grey steps, with no grain or texture dots on the body, and the door is a plain, flat panel. It is thinner and flatter than the references.
